main_issue: Who is responsible for the beef-contaminated shared pan, and whether the household should wash it, replace it, or split the cost of a new one so D can cook

A-B.evidence: Both deny cooking beef (1,2); A says 'Why should all of us have to pay' (15) and B 'I'm not paying for a new pan' (16).

A-C.evidence: C wants the pan dealt with and proposes washing rule (3,7); A only denies and challenges ('So?' 5), rejects shared payment (15); little shared ground.

A-D.evidence: D demands whoever used it replace it (10), then all chip in (14); A: 'We don't even know who used it' (11) and 'That's not fair' (15).

B-C.evidence: B asks others to sort it out (6) and refuses to pay (16); C's washing-rule proposal (7) never addressed by B.

B-D.evidence: D proposes all chip in for a new pan (14); B replies 'I'm not paying for a new pan' (16).

C-D.evidence: C offers to wash the pan (7), D says it doesn't help (8), C concedes 'I didn't think of that' (9) and asks what to do; no agreement on replacement.
